rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while respecting the workload: this shootout benchmark is dominated by tiny, hot-loop functions (total text only ~1.7 KB; test_lists, heapsort, matrix, hash run in tight loops), so BCF and FLA get the highest SecurityGain weights to flatten control flow and break loop-structure recognition in exactly the functions a reverser would target first, but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights stay mid-range so the selector still prefers cheaper passes for the smallest functions. SUB is weighted high on SecurityGain/DiversityGain with low CorrectnessRisk since arithmetic substitution is safe and cheap for the arithmetic-heavy kernels (hash, heapsort, matrix). IBR keeps a high SizeCost weight because indirect branching bloats many tiny basic blocks quickly, while its security value justifies use on the larger functions. SPLIT stays a low-cost enhancer (cheap, safe) that improves FLA/BCF effectiveness. ICALL and IGV round out diversity against static call-graph and global-variable analysis with minimal loop-overhead and near-zero runtime cost respectively; moderate CorrectnessRisk weights on FLA/ICALL reflect the main correctness hazards seen in pointer-heavy list code, letting the selector skip them where features look fragile.
